methods.V: Classify the single claim using only the supplied pinned source. SUPPORTED means the source supports the complete claim; CONTRADICTED means the source directly conflicts with it; INSUFFICIENT means the selected source cannot establish it. Return the required JSON, quoting relevant source when available. Do not claim runtime tests ran.
methods.R: Classify the single claim using only the supplied pinned source. Check the exact subject and lexical owner, declared type versus value, factory versus returned callback, local variable versus object property, read versus write, sync versus async path, and conditional versus universal scope. Citation membership alone is not support. SUPPORTED requires the complete relationship and qualifications; CONTRADICTED requires a source conflict; otherwise use INSUFFICIENT. Missing global evidence proves neither a universal claim nor its negation. Return the required JSON with exact source evidence when available. Do not claim runtime tests ran.

control_design: Two supported, two contradicted and two insufficient controls per development-exposed task. No general accuracy/holdout/fine-tuning claim. Distinct controls; same exact source/claim/schema/options between methods except system instruction. Order fixed V then R across all18; latency/cache/order effects not causal speed comparisons.
evaluation: Preserve transport/length/schema failures in operational denominator. Report semantic matrix for returned valid label separately. False support=(C or I predicted S)/(12C/I), false rejection=S predicted C/6S, supported abstention=S predicted I/6S, justified abstention=I predicted I/6I; zero denominator null. Require manual evidence/reason review; a correct label can have wrong evidence. Whole-document acceptance not measured.
